name: OSWorld
summary: Execution-based evaluation of agents performing tasks in real desktop environments.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Task-specific execution-based evaluators inspect application or system state.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Counts were computed from unique task identifiers in the two inspected manifests. The subsets differ; record the manifest, repository revision, agent interface, and step budget with a score.

name: WebArena
summary: Self-hosted web environments and tasks for evaluating autonomous web agents.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Functional correctness of completed web tasks.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The canonical repository documents self-hosted websites and environment resets. Its README recommends BrowserGym/AgentLab for newer infrastructure; harness changes must be recorded.

name: VisualWebArena
summary: Visually grounded web tasks extending the WebArena evaluation setting.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Execution-based completion checks for visually grounded web tasks.

counts.population: one task from each template type

benchmark_protocol.notes: The 233 demonstration trajectories are not the full 910-task evaluation set. Observation modes and captioning components differ across baseline agents.

name: AndroidWorld
summary: Android environment with programmatic task evaluation for mobile agents.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Programmatic task-specific initialization, system-state success checks, and teardown.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Random parameters produce many instances from the same task definitions. Preserve seeds and parameterization; 116 is not a count of all possible task instances.

name: Windows Agent Arena
summary: Windows 11 benchmark for multimodal desktop agents in a reproducible VM that runs locally or in parallel on Azure ML, with a harder mode where agents must set tasks up themselves.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Task configuration selects an evaluator and expected application or system outcome; evaluators return a reward for the resulting state.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Counted unique identifiers in the inspected manifest. Normal and hard modes differ in how much task setup the agent must perform. Record the difficulty and observation/backend configuration with each result; no VM was launched.

name: ScreenSpot Pro
summary: GUI grounding benchmark focused on professional high-resolution interfaces.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: For positive targets, the predicted point must fall inside the annotated bounding box.

counts.population: sum of icon/text counts in the published card table

benchmark_protocol.notes: Language, instruction style, and positive/negative target configuration are explicit evaluator options. This profile describes target localization, not end-to-end workflow completion. The target count is computed from the card table, not from expanded language/style evaluation instances.

name: OSWorld-G
summary: Computer-use grounding benchmark with original and refined instructions, released with the Jedi synthetic data pipeline, a 4-million-example Jedi dataset and Jedi-3B and Jedi-7B models.

actions: refusal represented by negative coordinates in the evaluator
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The inspected Jedi runner maps predictions from resized-image coordinates back to the original image, then checks the predicted center against rectangle/polygon targets or the refusal rule. It reports overall and classification-group accuracy. This is offline grounding, not OSWorld task-execution success.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The repository retains original OSWorld-G.json and refined OSWorld-G_refined.json instructions; treat them as alternative benchmark versions, not additional disjoint tasks. Refined instructions reduce requirements beyond grounding. The same repository also contains Jedi training/rendering material, which is excluded from benchmark counts. The standalone generic eval.py entry point is a stub; the named model runner supplies image_size to its geometry helper. No task count or successful execution is inferred from repository file totals. Apache-2.0 is recorded for code only.

name: WorkArena
summary: Browser-based enterprise workflow tasks built around ServiceNow.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Task-specific checks on ServiceNow workflows; levels and task configurations define different evaluations.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Definitions and instantiated tasks are different units. ServiceNow instance access is gated. WorkArena-L1 and WorkArena++ should be reported separately.

name: WebVoyager
summary: Multimodal web navigation agent and evaluation tasks on real websites.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The repository supplies an automated multimodal-model evaluation protocol.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The GAIA-derived subset is separate from the 643 WebVoyager queries. Live sites and time-sensitive travel tasks can change; record the task snapshot and evaluation date.

name: WebLINX
summary: Demonstrations and evaluation for conversational web navigation.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Offline evaluation compares action predictions against recorded human demonstrations.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The figures are rounded descriptions from the original paper. WebLINX 1.1 / BrowserGym removes some demonstrations and changes evaluated steps, including tab actions; do not mix those results or counts with the original release. This profile does not treat replayed demonstration steps as live task completion.

name: Mind2Web
summary: Human demonstrations and tasks for generalist web navigation research.

focus: generalization to unseen sites and domains
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Offline candidate and action evaluation against recorded demonstrations; the repository distinguishes macro from micro averaging.
benchmark_protocol.notes: These are reported split inventories, not online task-success measurements. Original Mind2Web, Multimodal-Mind2Web, and Online-Mind2Web have different inputs/protocols. The authors require macro-average metrics for comparison with the paper; test archives remain upstream.

name: Online Mind2Web
summary: 300 tasks on 136 live websites for evaluating web agents online, with outdated tasks replaced over time, human-reviewed submissions and the WebJudge automatic evaluator.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Human evaluation and WebJudge-based evaluation are documented as distinct assessment paths.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Tasks are actively replaced when websites or requirements become invalid. Record the task revision and submission schema; a constant headline task count does not imply an unchanged test set.

name: WebShop
summary: Simulated shopping environment for instruction-following web agents.

benchmark_protocol.notes: This is a simulated shop. The default preview loads 1,000 products, while the full inventory is much larger; report the loaded subset and observation mode. Instructions and products are different populations. Detailed reward semantics are not normalized in this profile.

name: BrowserGym
summary: Unified interfaces for browser-agent tasks and benchmark environments.

focus: benchmark adapters with separate task definitions
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Gymnasium reset/step interface delegates reward, completion, messages and task info to each adapter’s validate() method. There is no universal BrowserGym success metric or shared task total; retain benchmark/adapter version and action subset for comparisons.
benchmark_protocol.notes: A framework with interactive browser adapters and a static WebLINX evaluation integration, so the profile setting is mixed. README-listed integrations are not added as disjoint tasks or datasets. Core requires Playwright/Chromium; individual benchmarks have their own setup, credentials, licenses and validation rules. Apache-2.0 covers repository code only. No browser tasks or third-party project code were executed.

name: CRAB
summary: Cross-environment benchmark framework for multimodal agents.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Graph-based evaluators measure progress through task requirements.
benchmark_protocol.notes: CRAB is also an extensible framework. The 120-task count belongs to Benchmark-v0, not every environment that can be created with the framework.

name: AndroidLab
summary: Reproducible Android benchmark of 138 tasks across nine apps on predefined virtual devices, run via AVD on Mac or Docker on Linux, released with the Android Instruct training set.

actions: Android operations through the agent framework
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The evaluation pipeline produces success, subgoal success, reversed redundancy, and reasonable-operation metrics; result generation requires a configured judge model.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The benchmark uses predefined virtual-device images and apps chosen to work without network/login requirements. XML and SoM modes should be reported separately. These counts concern evaluation tasks, not the separately released Android Instruct training set.

name: AndroidArena
summary: Android environment for evaluating language-model-driven agents.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The released evaluator compares trajectories with reference actions using longest-common-subsequence-based task reward and completion. Its reversed redundancy metric is the reference/predicted action-length ratio (with 1e-6 denominator smoothing), multiplied by the LLM success flag. LLM success judgments and instruction-constraint checks are separate metrics. Full reference-dependent evaluation coverage cannot be assumed because complete annotated action sequences are not released.
benchmark_protocol.notes: README states that task instructions are released but annotated action sequences, apart from the calendar example, will come later. Environment setup targets Android API 33 with uiautomator2 and manual Google-account setup. Public task YAML and evaluator code exist, but benchmark execution and full reference coverage were not verified. No task total is derived from app YAML file counts. Code and data licenses remain unknown.

name: SPA-Bench
summary: 340 single-app and cross-app tasks over 66 Chinese and English Android apps, with plug-in support for 11 smartphone agents and automatic coarse-to-fine success detection.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: A multimodal evaluator and annotated key-component matching assess completion; the framework also reports resource-use metrics.

counts.population: README total including third-party, Google, and system apps

benchmark_protocol.notes: The two task subsets partition the 340 tasks. The integrated agent and evaluator modes must accompany results. The preconfigured emulator snapshot is still marked coming soon in the inspected documentation.

name: MobileAgentBench
summary: Automated benchmark for mobile LLM agents whose default tasks use ten Simple Mobile Tools Android apps, installed as a Python library that detects task completion.

name: MobileWorldBench
summary: Benchmark of semantic world modeling for mobile agents, with question-answering tasks and GPT-judged generation tasks, plus training data built on AitW and AndroidControl screens.

name: MobileSafetyBench
summary: Android emulator testbed that scores mobile device-control agents on both safety and helpfulness, using ADB and Appium for observations, actions and success checks.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Appium-backed task evaluators track goal achievement and harm prevention as separate booleans, plus risk-detection step and completion progress. The base evaluator defaults to max_step=15; task-specific overrides must be retained. Results are not a single generic success-rate metric.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Inspected release/ver.3 branch exposes task definitions, Android environment and per-task evaluators. It requires Android API 34, Appium/ADB and documented third-party app versions; those APKs/accounts were not acquired. The action parser includes semantic shortcuts in addition to screen gestures, so this is not a strictly coordinate-only action setting. No corpus task total is inferred from evaluator-module or file counts. Apache-2.0 applies to repository code, not automatically app/data assets.

name: B-MoCA
summary: Mobile control benchmark with varied interface configurations.

actions: normalized touch/lift coordinate pairs for tap or swipe
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Task success is detected using Appium; positive task reward terminates the episode. Environment variants change device/locale/wallpaper/DPI/dark mode and are loaded as snapshots. The numeric action interface is (touch_y, touch_x, lift_y, lift_x); wrapper/tanh transformations must be kept with the evaluated agent.

counts.population: asset/tasks/**/*.textproto in retained release/ver.3 tree; not a paper test-task total

benchmark_protocol.notes: Current source inventory differs in grain from published experiment subsets: do not multiply 131 definitions by 35/10 configuration rows or label the product as evaluated tasks. Setup requires Android API 29, Appium, external app versions and generated AVD snapshots. No apps/snapshots were downloaded or run. Code Apache-2.0 does not establish data or app rights.

name: LlamaTouch
summary: Mobile UI task evaluation using application state information.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Checks whether the recorded execution visits all annotated essential states rather than requiring an identical action sequence.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Application coverage refers to the self-constructed subset. Task execution and essential-state annotation are separate components; counts are publisher-reported, not a fresh task-file recount.

name: VisualWebBench
summary: Evaluation of multimodal models on visual web understanding tasks.

name: VideoGUI
summary: Benchmark for desktop GUI tasks derived from instructional videos.

name: WorldGUI
summary: 611 desktop GUI tasks that agents must complete from varied starting points, shipped with instructional videos and project files, plus the self-reflective WorldGUI-Agent baseline.

name: ScienceBoard
summary: Scientific-workflow tasks for multimodal agents in desktop software such as ChimeraX, KAlgebra, Celestia, Grass GIS and Lean 4, with apps modified to expose state for evaluation.

actions: code/tool commands and answer/stop actions according to configured agent mode
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Application-specific verifiers inspect state, files, database values, equations, compilation or answer/stop conditions. The official audit records 242 verifier entries across its VM task suite. This profile covers the released VM task definitions; Docker smoke results and Raw/Dual alternatives are separate populations.

counts.population: tasks/VM/**/*.json at tree 21b5eb0f; excludes tasks/Raw and tasks/Dual
VM suite: Celestia, ChimeraX, GrassGIS, KAlgebra, Lean, TeXstudio

benchmark_protocol.notes: Manifest count 169 matches the official verifier audit. Other Raw/Dual definitions can represent alternative execution modes of the same problems and are not added. Official Docker migration documents a 20-task acceptance subset, not a full-suite performance result; legacy VMware remains. External service sign-in/rate limits, amd64 binaries and ChimeraX redistribution terms limit portability. Only code MIT is established; VM, scientific data and bundled apps need their own terms.

name: Spider2-V
summary: Visual agent evaluation on data-science and engineering workflows.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Task-specific evaluation functions are invoked after agent execution.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Counted unique task IDs in the full manifest. Verbose versus abstract instructions and account versus non-account tasks form different subsets. The Ubuntu VM and external-account requirements are part of the protocol; no accounts or environments were provisioned.

name: MMInA
summary: Multimodal web tasks in a WebArena-based environment that chain from 1 to 10 hops across sites such as a shopping store and Wikipedia, testing long-chain reasoning.

name: MMBench-GUI
summary: Four-level GUI-agent benchmark across six platforms, from content understanding and element grounding to task automation and collaboration, scored with an efficiency-quality area metric.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Level-specific evaluation; Efficiency–Quality Area (EQA) combines navigation quality and efficiency.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The README documents four levels, but its release notes and TODOs distinguish released L1/L2 evaluation from pending L3/L4 integration. Do not treat every level as the same evaluator or a complete implemented interface.

name: GUIHalluBench
summary: Measures hallucination in UI-element parsing by matching the boxes and descriptions a model lists for 1,000 English and 1,000 Chinese screenshots against human annotations.

actions: list of UI element boxes [x1,y1,x2,y2] and text descriptions
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Metrics use greedy one-to-one matching in descending IoU order, then micro precision/recall/F1 and lowercased difflib.SequenceMatcher description similarity on matched pairs. Actual metrics.py accepts IoU >= 0.5 at its default threshold; README prose says > 0.5. Predictions align to annotations by image_path; callers must supply complete prediction coverage because missing predictions are not independently enumerated by evaluate_dataset.

counts.population: English annotation subset reported by README
Chinese annotation subset reported by README

benchmark_protocol.notes: Each annotation entry represents a page, not one UI element. README’s illustrative num_samples=4796 output is not adopted as a corpus count. Public tree contains both annotation JSON files and an images.tar.gz Git-LFS pointer; payload availability/integrity was not tested by downloading images. LEGAL.md only governs comment-language precedence, not a code/data license grant; both slots remain unknown. No benchmark run was performed.

name: VeriWeb (formerly VeriGUI)
summary: Verifiable web information-seeking benchmark renamed from VeriGUI; desktop evaluation is described as future work.

name: WindowsWorld
summary: Cross-application Windows benchmark with intermediate task evaluation.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Publisher distinguishes S_int (intermediate checkpoint score on L1–L3) and S_final (final completion on L1–L4). Documented step budgets are 15/25/40/20 for L1/L2/L3/L4. Preserve level, observation mode, agent interface and checkpoint/final metric when reporting a run.

counts.population: WindowsWorld benchmark described in the retained README
WindowsWorld coverage described in the retained README

benchmark_protocol.notes: Interactive VMware/Windows environment. The public repository includes benchmark.json, task/evaluator code and monitoring support; the README refers VM import to Installation Guide.md, whose distribution links and payloads were not inspected for this profile. Checkpoint counts and application counts are not extra tasks. Apache-2.0 is recorded for repository code; Windows, apps and VM artifacts retain separate terms.

name: MacAgentBench
summary: 676 macOS tasks across 25 applications, each run in its own Docker container and scored by deterministic rule-based checks with multiple checkpoints.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Deterministic rule-based evaluators with intermediate checkpoints.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The benchmark evaluates multiple agent frameworks and GUI/CLI workflows. Framework skills and interfaces affect the task setting; the inspected README does not define one universal observation representation.

name: RiOSWorld
summary: Measures risky behavior of multimodal computer-use agents in an Ubuntu virtual machine, with risk scenarios such as phishing emails and released evaluation trajectories.

name: SaaS-Bench
summary: 106 browser-driven business workflows across 23 self-hosted SaaS apps in six domains, scored by per-task verifiers that read each app's database and give partial credit.

name: MCPWorld
summary: Evaluation environment combining computer interaction with tool access.
notes: The retained paper reports 201 tasks, whereas the retained repository README describes approximately 170. These are separate source descriptions; their release/version difference has not been established.

name: Precision CUA Bench
summary: Evaluation resources for pixel-precise cursor grounding in code editors.

observations: red-cross feedback marking previous incorrect prediction
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The inspected evaluator scales target boxes from a 1000×1000 reference grid into image pixels and tests pixel predictions, allowing ±10 pixels around the center along any target dimension narrower than 1 pixel after scaling. It reports cumulative hit accuracy by turn (earlier hits remain correct), miss distances, any-turn hit rate, and a correction rate whose denominator is all successfully processed samples. The default budget is five turns; retain prompt/feedback variant, turn budget, and processed/skipped coverage.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The release has four editor/theme JSONL partitions (Cursor/VS Code × dark/light) and screenshot files. Partitions are not train/test splits or independent task totals. README’s initial field table calls bbox pixel coordinates, but the evaluation-format section and actual ratio_h/ratio_w=dimension/1000 code use normalized target boxes; profile follows the inspected evaluator and retains the inconsistency. Source/images were not executed or downloaded as a dataset. MIT is recorded for repository code only.

name: WebGames
summary: 150 client-side web challenges in five capability domains, built to be easy for humans but hard for browsing agents, each revealing a password when solved.

name: WebCanvas
summary: Framework and evaluation resources for real-world web agents.

name: UI-TARS
summary: Native GUI agent models; UI-TARS-1.5 adds reinforcement-learned reasoning before acting and an open 7B checkpoint, and UI-TARS-2 extends to games, code and tool use.

name: OpenCUA
summary: Open computer-use research stack including models and training resources.

name: UI-Venus
summary: GUI agent model family; UI-Venus-2, at 9B and 27B, acts on mobile, web and desktop in one end-to-end agent, trained with keypoint-based multi-judge task verification.

name: EvoCUA
summary: Computer-use model and training resources from the EvoCUA project.

name: ScaleCUA
summary: Computer-use model family trained with cross-platform interaction data.

name: CogAgent
summary: Visual language model for GUI understanding and interaction.

name: OS-Atlas
summary: OS-Atlas GUI action models, including grounding bases fine-tuned from InternVL2-4B and Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct that accept any image size and output 0-1000 relative coordinates.

name: SeeClick
summary: GUI grounding model trained to locate visual interface elements.

name: UGround
summary: Code, training data and weights for universal visual grounding of GUI elements from screenshots, including Qwen2-VL-based UGround-V1 at 2B, 7B and 72B and offline and online evaluation suites.

name: ShowUI
summary: Lightweight GUI-agent vision-language-action model from Show Lab and Microsoft, released with UI-guided token selection, training code, the ShowUI-web and ShowUI-desktop datasets and vLLM inference.

name: Aguvis
summary: Vision-based GUI agent models with unified action representations.

name: GUI-Actor
summary: GUI grounding model with attention-based action localization.

name: Phi-Ground
summary: Microsoft GUI grounding models from an empirical study of grounding training, from data collection to model training, released as Phi-Ground-4B-7C with evaluation code.

name: Fara
summary: Microsoft browser-use agent models that act from screenshots by predicting click coordinates without accessibility trees; Fara1.5 comes in 4B, 9B and 27B, succeeding Fara-7B.

name: AgentCPM-GUI
summary: 8B on-device smartphone agent built on MiniCPM-V that operates Chinese and English apps from screenshots, trained with reinforcement fine-tuning and a compact JSON action space.

name: POINTS-GUI
summary: POINTS-GUI-G-8B GUI grounding model, trained from a POINTS-1.5 base without native grounding through a data pipeline that unifies coordinates, filters noise and adds hard cases.

name: UI-R1
summary: Rule-based reinforcement learning for GUI action prediction, releasing UI-R1-3B, trained from Qwen2.5-VL-3B, the efficiency-oriented UI-R1-E-3B, and training data.

name: InfiGUI-R1
summary: 3B GUI agent trained in two stages: distilling spatial reasoning from teacher models, then reinforcement learning that rewards accurate sub-goals and trains error recovery.

name: InfiGUI-G1
summary: InfiGUI-G1 3B and 7B grounding models trained with Adaptive Exploration Policy Optimization, which samples several candidate answers per pass under an adaptive exploration reward.

name: GUI-G2
summary: GUI grounding models at 3B and 7B trained with Gaussian rewards for click proximity to element centers and region coverage, with variance scaled to element size.

name: UI-AGILE
summary: GUI agent trained by RL with a continuous reward, a simple-thinking reward and cropping-based resampling on about 9k samples, plus a plug-in decomposed grounding-and-selection inference method.

name: Aria-UI
summary: Mixture-of-experts GUI grounding model with 3.9B activated parameters that can use text or interleaved image history, with released training data and an AndroidWorld agent.

name: Ferret-UI
summary: Screen understanding research within the Ferret model family.
notes: The repository has moved from apple/ml-ferret to apple-aiml-research/ml-ferret; evidence uses the dedicated ferretui component.

name: GELab Zero
summary: Open mobile GUI agent stack pairing a 4B model that runs on consumer hardware with local multi-device infrastructure, an MCP server, and AndroidDaily benchmark tasks.

name: DiMo-GUI
summary: GUI grounding research using modality-aware visual reasoning and test-time scaling.

name: TreeCUA
summary: Framework for generating GUI trajectories through tree-structured exploration and verification.

name: GUI-Odyssey
summary: Human-demonstrated Android episodes for cross-app navigation, spanning six task types, 212 apps and about 1,400 app combinations, for training and evaluating agents.

dataset_profile.notes: The repository gives conflicting episode totals (8,334 and 8,834). This profile uses 8,334 from the specifically recommended current dataset card. No independent archive recount was performed. Coordinates are normalized to 0–1000.

name: GUICourse
summary: Three datasets for turning general VLMs into GUI agents: GUIEnv for OCR and grounding, GUIAct with 67k single-step and 15k multi-step web and Android actions, and GUIChat dialogues.

name: AMEX
summary: Code for AMEX Android GUI data that converts its three annotation levels into question-answer pairs and fine-tunes a LLaMA2-Accessory model, with a released checkpoint.

counts.population: AMEX collection described in the paper

dataset_profile.notes: The main repository contains companion training code. The scale and annotation levels here come from the paper, not an independent download or completeness audit.

name: MoTIF
summary: Mobile task demonstrations and natural-language instructions.

dataset_profile.notes: The raw collection mixes action, language, exploration, and unusable/other traces. These groups have different annotation coverage; not every raw trace is a valid task demonstration.

name: Screen2Words
summary: Mobile screen descriptions for language-based screen understanding.

dataset_profile.notes: Multiple summaries describe one screen. The repository provides annotations and split files; use the referenced RICO assets for screenshots.

name: ScreenQA
summary: About 86,000 human-written question-answer pairs over 35,000 Rico mobile screenshots, plus ScreenQA Short and ComplexQA variants, for benchmarking screen content understanding.

dataset_profile.notes: All questions for a given screenshot share one split. ScreenQA Short reuses the same questions/screens; ComplexQA is a separate extension. Do not add these variants as independent original examples.

name: MultiUI
summary: 7.3 million training samples built from webpage UIs and structured with enhanced accessibility trees, for text-rich visual understanding, released with UIX-Qwen2 models.

dataset_profile.notes: The README provides a rounded sample count. It does not establish a unique-screenshot inventory or a normalized split breakdown. Synthetic examples and publicly sourced web content have provenance and quality limits; data terms must be checked separately from repository code.

name: OS-Genesis
summary: Interaction-driven pipeline that synthesizes mobile and web GUI agent trajectories without human supervision or predefined tasks, via reverse task synthesis and a trajectory reward model.

dataset_profile.notes: The repository links distinct AndroidControl-oriented, AndroidWorld-oriented, and web training files plus raw pre-state/action/post-state triples. These are training artifacts, not a documented train/test split, and related representations are not disjoint corpus totals. No numerical inventory is asserted from release names or linked archives.

name: AgentTrek
summary: Synthesizes browser-agent trajectories by replaying web tutorials as guidance, releasing the trajectory data with multimodal grounding and reasoning and an AgentTrek-32B agent.

name: GUI-World
summary: GUI video benchmark and training data covering six scenarios, from Android and iOS to websites and XR, with eight question types for image and video LLMs and the GUI-Vid model.

dataset_profile.notes: Taxonomy counts describe coverage, not the number of videos or questions. Cases include Android, iOS, desktop software, websites, multi-application use, and XR. Keyframe-selection settings affect evaluation; exact sample inventories are not reported here.

name: GUI-Action Narrator
summary: Action narration resources for GUI interaction trajectories.
notes: Original repository URL redirects to showlab/GUI-Narrator.

counts.population: Act2Cap benchmark described in the paper

dataset_profile.notes: A captioning sample is not necessarily a unique video or complete task trajectory. Package layout and split sizes were not established by the inspected sources.

name: RoTS
summary: Announced GUI trajectory synthesis resources for recovery from policy-induced errors; the inspected repository marks code and data releases as in preparation.

counts.population: paper-described synthesis output; not a released file inventory

dataset_profile.notes: The inspected README marks the dataset and collection pipelines as in preparation. This profile records an announced research asset, not a verified downloadable corpus; file formats, splits, and release-specific data terms remain unknown.

details.availability: announced; data and sampling pipelines in preparation

notes: The 800k figure describes training samples in the study, not an independently counted public download. The repository code-license declaration does not establish terms for an unreleased dataset.

name: FingerTip-20K
summary: Over 20,000 human Android episodes across 500+ apps with user context and long-term usage patterns, plus tracks for proactive intent prediction and personalized execution.

name: UI-Ins
summary: Treats grounding instructions as multiple reasoning perspectives, releasing a data pipeline, training code and UI-Ins-7B and 32B models trained by SFT on synthesized instructions, then RL.

name: Agent S
summary: Simular's open-source framework for computer-use agents that click, type and scroll through desktop and web apps on macOS, Windows and Linux; its third generation, Agent S3, reports 72.6% on OSWorld.

name: UI-TARS Desktop
summary: Desktop app for a local GUI agent driven by UI-TARS and Seed-1.5-VL/1.6 models, offering local and remote operators for computers and browsers; the repository also ships the Agent TARS CLI and web UI.

name: Mobile-Agent
summary: Mobile device agent family using visual interface interaction.
notes: This repository contains multiple Mobile-Agent generations. Platform coverage differs by version; use the corresponding paper and implementation instructions.

name: AppAgent
summary: Multimodal agent that operates Android apps through taps and swipes without back-end access, building a reusable knowledge base from autonomous exploration or from watching human demonstrations.

name: AppAgentX
summary: Mobile agent research using accumulated interaction experience.

name: AppAgent Pro
summary: Proactive Android agent built on AppAgent that uses GPT-4o to decide whether YouTube or Amazon content would help, operates those apps over ADB, and merges what it finds into its answer.

name: AutoDroid
summary: LLM-powered Android task automation built on DroidBot, released with DroidTask, a dataset of per-app screenshots, view hierarchies, exploration records and ground-truth task files.

name: AutoDroid V2
summary: An Android automation implementation that builds app documentation from exploration traces and evaluates language-model-generated execution code in emulator workflows.
notes: The repository uses README_minimal.md rather than README.md and includes a documented App Launcher experiment, training setup and DroidTask/LlamaTouch evaluation scripts. Its supplied emulator setup targets x86_64 Linux and Android API 31. No repository-level code license was found; code, APK, data and weight terms are not inferred from one another. Dependencies, external evaluation files and model service are still required; no software was run.

details.availability: Public source and minimal-experiment documentation are released; default README path is absent.

name: UFO
summary: Windows agent framework for application and desktop automation.

name: MagenticLite / Magentic UI
summary: Microsoft agent application combining orchestration with browser interaction; successor to Magentic UI.

name: OS-Copilot
summary: Open-source library for generalist agents acting on an operating system's web, terminals, files and third-party apps, with the FRIDAY assistant, which takes custom tools and self-learns Excel tasks.

name: Cradle
summary: Framework in which foundation models control games and software from screenshots alone, acting through keyboard and mouse, shown on RDR2, Stardew Valley, Cities: Skylines and Dealer's Life 2.

name: AssistGUI
summary: LLM-based assistant for automating work in desktop productivity software by watching the screen and issuing mouse and keyboard commands; its repository says the code will be released later.

name: ScreenAgent
summary: Environment and agent in which a vision-language model controls real desktops over VNC with mouse and keyboard in plan, act and reflect stages, plus a hand-annotated dataset of daily computer tasks.

name: SeeAct
summary: Generalist web agent framework for large multimodal models such as GPT-4V, with a Playwright tool that runs agents on live websites, text-choice and set-of-mark grounding, and a crawler mode.

name: Agent E
summary: Browser automation agent on the AG2 framework that pairs a planner agent with a browser navigation agent to fill forms, search shops and work through sites, also callable over a local HTTP API.

name: PC-Agent
summary: Human-cognition-transfer framework for PC agents: PC Tracker logs human computer use, cognition completion turns logs into cognitive trajectories, and a planner works with a grounding agent.

name: Open Interpreter
summary: Assistant framework combining code execution and computer interaction.
notes: The repository has evolved substantially; computer-use functionality is documented in its Computer Use section. Do not infer parity with historical releases.

name: Self Operating Computer

actions: predicted click point; a predicted box is reduced to its center

focus: single-step GUI grounding on the ScreenSpot-v2 release

This is a named compatible evaluator implementation; the OS-Atlas dataset card itself supplies no evaluator specification.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The public Hub revision 5efbb1f1 contains three platform JSON annotation files and an image ZIP; its card only declares Apache-2.0. Files were listed, not downloaded as data.

name: OmniAct
summary: Dataset and benchmark for generating computer interaction programs.

actions: PyAutoGUI script: pointer movement/click/drag, key presses, hotkeys, and text entry
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: The bundled evaluator reports weighted sequence match and action match, comparing action types and applying coordinate, key, and writing penalties. Target element-box metadata is evaluation-only. The retained scorer has a click-penalty defect: predicted coordinates are read from gold_line, so score reproduction requires explicit scorer-version review.
benchmark_protocol.notes: This released split table totals 9,799 examples; it is not silently substituted for any paper-level collection size. Public files include train/test/val JSON indexes, task/image archives, and eval.py. Evaluation is offline script comparison, not execution success on a live desktop. benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Automated LLM judge scores both task accuracy and safety from saved execution traces. Keep judge model/prompt version and harm category with a result; the scripts separately compute predicted metrics. This is an interactive desktop safety benchmark, not a single offline grounding score.

released misuse task-ID list; before injection/goal expansion
released injection task-ID list; before injection/goal expansion

benchmark_protocol.notes: README/paper reports 150 tasks, whereas retained misuse/injection/misbehavior lists contain 50/10/50 IDs. run.py expands injection vectors/goals, so the released ID inventory is not a direct recount of paper settings; the complete expanded total was not reconstructed. Judge agreement F1 values in the README measure agreement with human labels, not agent success. Experiments use OSWorld desktop apps, with VMware documented as tested and screenshot/a11y/SOM observation choices. Code Apache-2.0 does not establish VM/app/data rights. Publisher asks that the benchmark not be used directly as agent training data.

notes: The retained task-ID manifests have 50 misuse, 10 injection and 50 misbehavior IDs. Prompt-injection execution expands vectors/goals; the reported 150-task total must not be read as 150 unique released IDs.
