name: Computer-Using World Model
summary: Presents a desktop world model that predicts textual UI changes before synthesizing the next screenshot. It learns from Microsoft Office transitions and is evaluated by letting a frozen agent compare simulated actions before execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning for continual GUI learning, using policy entropy to adjust their proportions and gradient projection to limit conflicting updates. AndroidControl-CL groups applications into sequential tasks to evaluate adaptation and retention.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract describes artifact release as future work; this annotation does not assert current availability.

name: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks
summary: Studies webpage injections that affect both screenshots and accessibility trees, then trains web agents through teacher imitation, supervised adversarial examples, and adversarial reinforcement learning. The evaluation tests defenses on MiniWoB++ and held-out tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Generalization in Online Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Agents
summary: Introduces AndroidWorld-Generalization with separate tests for unseen task instances, templates, and applications. A GRPO training system combines containerized environments with asynchronous trajectory collection to study these generalization regimes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: OSExpert: Computer-Use Agents Learning Professional Skills via Exploration
summary: Uses GUI-based depth-first exploration to verify elementary software functions, assemble action primitives, and construct curricula of composed skills. OSExpert-Eval examines how the resulting procedural knowledge supports complex computer-use tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: SecAgent: Efficient Mobile GUI Agent with Semantic Context
summary: Presents a Chinese mobile GUI dataset and navigation benchmark together with SecAgent, which compresses previous screenshots and actions into semantic summaries. The agent is trained with supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning to use this compact interaction context.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Mobile use is explicit, but the abstract does not identify a mobile operating system.

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
summary: Introduces VeriEnv, which recreates websites as executable training environments and exposes internal state through a Python SDK for task generation and deterministic reward checks. Experiments examine web-agent learning across new and expanded site environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract promises a release upon acceptance; this annotation does not verify artifact availability.

name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: AdaZoom-GUI: Adaptive Zoom-based GUI Grounding with Instruction Refinement
summary: Combines instruction rewriting with conditional second-stage zooming for small GUI targets. A grounding dataset and GRPO training support joint prediction of click coordinates and element bounding boxes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: OS-Themis: A Scalable Critic Framework for Generalist GUI Rewards
summary: Presents OS-Themis, a multi-agent critic that divides GUI trajectories into verifiable milestones and reviews their evidence before assigning an outcome. OGRBench evaluates GUI rewards across platforms, with AndroidWorld experiments examining training and trajectory filtering.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
summary: Turns draft web-agent skills into structured executable artifacts that support deterministic checks, fault localization and local repair. VisualWebArena and MiniWoB experiments examine execution and reuse within the same benchmark family.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract limits its portability evidence to transfer within a benchmark family, not generalization across arbitrary benchmarks.

name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
summary: Audits sources of ambiguity and operational variation in WebVoyager evaluation and introduces standardized guidance for task setup, failure handling, annotation and reporting. Emergence WebVoyager applies this protocol to a web-agent evaluation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations instead of direct memory access. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: IntentScore: Intent-Conditioned Action Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Trains IntentScore on offline desktop GUI interactions to assess candidate actions using both their state relevance and planning intent. The reward model is evaluated as an action reranker for Agent S3 on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Don't Act Blindly: Robust GUI Automation via Action-Effect Verification and Self-Correction
summary: Introduces VeriGUI, which checks expected action effects and reasons about recovery before subsequent GUI actions. Training combines synthetic failure trajectories with verification-weighted GRPO, evaluated on an AndroidControl-based robustness benchmark.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: What's Missing in Screen-to-Action? Towards a UI-in-the-Loop Paradigm for Multimodal GUI Reasoning
summary: Introduces UILoop, which inserts explicit UI-element localization, function and usage reasoning between screen observation and action. UI Comprehension-Bench evaluates these element-level capabilities with three metrics.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Android Coach: Improve Online Agentic Training Efficiency with Single State Multiple Actions
summary: Introduces Android Coach, which uses a learned critic to evaluate multiple candidate actions at each observed emulator state. Process rewards and a group-wise advantage estimator support online training, evaluated on AndroidLab and AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract states that artifacts will be released; this annotation does not independently verify release status or licenses.

name: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
summary: Introduces CORA, which calibrates a risk model to choose between executing and abstaining from mobile GUI actions, then diagnoses rejected actions to suggest interventions. Phone-Harm provides step-level safety labels for evaluating this safeguarding process.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The annotation describes risk calibration without asserting an unconditional safety guarantee.

name: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
summary: Introduces HealthAdminBench with GUI environments for an electronic health record, payer portals and fax handling. Expert-defined administrative tasks are decomposed into verifiable subtasks to compare local progress with end-to-end workflow completion.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
summary: Presents WebForge, a pipeline that plans, generates, refines and validates self-contained interactive websites. WebForge-Bench uses these environments to evaluate browser agents across domains and controlled difficulty levels.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ClawGUI: A Unified Framework for Training, Evaluating, and Deploying GUI Agents
summary: Presents ClawGUI, a shared harness for GUI-agent reinforcement learning, benchmark evaluation and deployment on mobile devices. It combines parallel virtual and physical environments, process rewards, and hybrid CLI-GUI execution with persistent memory.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: PrecisionCUA: Iterative Visual Refinement for Pixel-Precise Cursor Grounding in Code Editors
summary: Studies iterative cursor grounding in dense code-editor interfaces, using visual feedback from earlier attempts to correct displacement. PrecisionCUA evaluates this closed-loop process across multiple model families on coding-interface tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces UI-Zoomer, a training-free grounding method that uses candidate agreement and token confidence to decide when to crop and retry. Prediction variance determines a separate crop radius for each uncertain interface target.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
summary: Introduces GUI-Perturbed, which varies screenshot appearance and instruction wording independently to diagnose grounding failures. Experiments on three related model architectures examine relational instructions, browser zoom and augmentation-based fine-tuning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: FedGUI: Benchmarking Federated GUI Agents across Heterogeneous Platforms, Devices, and Operating Systems
summary: Introduces FedGUI, a federated GUI-learning benchmark built from six datasets spanning mobile, web and desktop interfaces. Its experiments separate platform, device, operating-system and data-source heterogeneity when evaluating collaborative training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
summary: Presents OpenMobile, which builds exploration-based environment memory to synthesize task instructions and switches between learner and expert policies during trajectory collection. The resulting data includes recovery behavior and is tested through mobile-agent training and benchmark-overlap analysis.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: HalluClear: Diagnosing, Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucinations in GUI Agents
summary: Introduces HalluClear with a GUI hallucination taxonomy, expert-calibrated evaluation workflow and structured-reasoning post-training scheme. It evaluates how these components affect hallucinations, grounding and action fidelity across GUI agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Measure Twice, Click Once: Co-evolving Proposer and Visual Critic via Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding
summary: Trains a GUI grounding proposer together with a visual critic that evaluates candidate locations rendered on screenshots. An adaptive reinforcement-learning schedule balances their development, using proposal diversity and critic feedback during training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
summary: Introduces Odysseys, a live-web benchmark of long, multi-site tasks derived from browsing sessions. Graded task rubrics and a rubric-score-per-step measure evaluate both partial progress and trajectory efficiency.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
summary: Introduces DynamicGUIBench for applications whose interfaces change between actions, together with DynamicUI, an agent that processes screen recordings. The agent selects informative frames, filters inconsistent action reasoning and uses trajectory reflection for subsequent decisions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments
summary: Introduces WindowsWorld for professional workflows spanning multiple desktop applications, with generated tasks refined through human review. Intermediate subgoals support process-oriented evaluation of cross-application reasoning and execution efficiency.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Desktop use is explicit; no additional operating-system claim is inferred solely from the benchmark name.

name: Faithful Mobile GUI Agents with Guided Advantage Estimator
summary: Introduces Faithful-Agent, which first teaches abstention under perturbed evidence and then refines GUI policies with an anchor-based, variance-adaptive advantage estimator. A thought-action consistency reward encourages decisions grounded in displayed evidence and instructions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
summary: Presents AutoFocus, a training-free grounding method that turns sampled coordinates and token uncertainty into spatial region proposals. Shape-aware crops and visual comparison select a target while retaining surrounding interface context.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
summary: Introduces Weblica, which combines HTTP-level capture and replay with website-grounded environment synthesis. The resulting interactive web environments support reinforcement learning and tests of navigation transfer and inference-time scaling.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
summary: Reorganizes webpage accessibility trees into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction. PageDigest supplies a persistent region-level observation to web agents, evaluated on WebArena.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
summary: Compares mobile world models that predict state changes as delta text, full text, images or renderable code. Downstream Android benchmarks examine synthetic training trajectories and test-time guidance, including limits of post-action reflection.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
summary: Trains GUI agents with a learned selector that removes repeated visual patches across consecutive screenshots while preserving spatial structure. ReVision evaluates this history representation on OSWorld, WebTailBench and AgentNetBench.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces OpenComputer, which builds desktop tasks around application-state verifiers and refines those verifiers using execution feedback. An evaluation harness records trajectories and assigns auditable partial credit across professional software workflows.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
summary: Introduces ScaleWoB, which synthesizes interactive GUI environments as backend-free webpages with verifiable rewards. Its mobile-oriented benchmark evaluates agent execution and compares selected synthetic tasks with real-app behavior.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Mobile, desktop and automotive interfaces are simulated as webpages; this does not assert native deployment on those platforms.

name: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Presents CUA-Gym, which co-generates instructions, initial and target states, and executable reward checks through generator-discriminator iterations. Mock web applications expand training environments, with learned agents evaluated on OSWorld-Verified and WebArena.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract promises future open sourcing; this annotation does not independently verify artifact release or licensing.

name: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research
summary: Introduces MobileGym, a browser-hosted simulation of mobile app interactions whose configurable JSON state supports deterministic judging and parallel rollouts. MobileGym-Bench adds parameterized tasks, with experiments examining online training and transfer to real devices.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The simulator is browser-hosted; the abstract does not identify a native mobile operating system.

name: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
summary: Introduces PhoneWorld, which converts observed app pages, transitions and state changes into executable Android environments through a build-inspect-repair process. Generated tasks and programmatic verifiers support benchmarking, trajectory collection and online training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent general computer-operation benchmark: the evaluated interface is a terminal; GUI benchmarks are a contrast, not its execution modality.

name: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward
summary: This survey organizes agent skills by architecture, acquisition, deployment and security, including their role in computer-use systems and GUI grounding. It also proposes a permission and lifecycle governance framework for skill deployment.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent survey of the skill layer: CUA deployment and GUI grounding are explicit parts of the review, but its overall scope extends well beyond interface agents.

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
summary: This study examines agent data injection, where untrusted content impersonates trusted metadata or tool-context data. It reports arbitrary-click vulnerabilities in web agents alongside separate coding-agent attacks, highlighting trust-boundary failures beyond instruction injection.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: DeskCraft: Benchmarking Desktop Agents on Professional Workflows and Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration
summary: DeskCraft evaluates professional desktop workflows and human-agent collaboration through mid-execution clarification, interruption and post-completion feedback. Its tasks cover creative applications and expose difficulties in long-horizon execution and proactive clarification.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: AJ-Bench: Benchmarking Agent-as-a-Judge for Environment-Aware Evaluation
summary: AJ-Bench evaluates judge agents that actively gather evidence from search, data systems and graphical interfaces. Its annotated tasks and trajectories test information acquisition, state verification and process verification.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent supervision interface: the browser UI is for human review of terminal agents; the abstract does not claim that those agents operate graphical interfaces.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.
verify_terms: Terminal Is All You Need: Design
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent conceptual HCI work about agent-facing interfaces; the abstract does not report GUI task experiments or a new evaluated CUA.

name: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
summary: CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
summary: VISTA evaluates coding agents that turn design handoffs into working web and Android applications. Its evaluator locates annotated interactive components and probes their behavior, keeping visual localization distinct from functional correctness.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent GUI-application generation benchmark with real component interaction probes; its main evaluated agents are application coders, not general GUI task executors.

name: MUIAnno: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for Mobile UI Understanding
summary: MUIAnno provides expert labels for elements in manually explored mobile-app screens, with a web annotation tool that emits structured JSON. It also supplies UI-element detection baselines for the dataset.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent computer-automation benchmark using terminal workflows, explicitly separated from graphical-interface control.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent cross-domain VLM compression method with actual GUI-benchmark evaluation; the abstract does not establish a full computer-use policy.

name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.

notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions rather than recall alone.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
summary: NestBrowse organizes browser actions in a nested framework that separates interaction control from page exploration. It evaluates this design for deep information seeking beyond snippet retrieval and direct URL fetching.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.

name: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: MMAC-Copilot: Multi-modal Agent Collaboration Operating Copilot

name: SmartFlow: Robotic Process Automation using LLMs
summary: Presents SmartFlow, which converts visible GUI elements into text for language-model action planning and executes the plan through a scripting engine. A collection of enterprise applications evaluates adaptation to different layouts and tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents by a Guard Agent via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
summary: Introduces GuardAgent, which translates safety requests into executable guardrail code using plans and retrieved demonstrations. Mind2Web-SC supplies a web-agent safety-policy evaluation alongside a separate healthcare access-control benchmark.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The web-agent evidence is Mind2Web-SC; the healthcare benchmark does not independently establish GUI control.

name: Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents
summary: Introduces adversarial tasks on VisualWebArena and an evaluation framework that tracks how manipulated information passes between agent components. The analysis examines vulnerabilities introduced by reflection and tree-search evaluators as well as direct action generation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Tree Search for Language Model Agents
summary: Applies best-first search to agent actions within interactive web environments, allowing exploration and multistep planning at inference time. WebArena and VisualWebArena experiments examine search behavior and test-time computation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Caution for the Environment: Multimodal LLM Agents are Susceptible to Environmental Distractions
summary: Measures how irrelevant GUI content affects multimodal agents using a simulated dataset and three perception patterns. The study also examines adversarial environment injection and possible ways to improve instruction faithfulness.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract describes a simulated dataset; real-browser deployment is not asserted.

name: The Impact of Element Ordering on LM Agent Performance
summary: Studies how the ordering of UI elements in an agent observation affects web and desktop performance. A pixel-based element detector and dimensionality-reduction ordering are evaluated on OmniACT when document hierarchy is unavailable.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Inferring Alt-text For UI Icons With Large Language Models During App Development
summary: Introduces IconDesc, which generates mobile icon alt-text from partial UI context such as element identifiers, bounds, nearby text and hierarchy. Model evaluation and a user study examine the resulting accessibility descriptions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. This is a UI accessibility and element-description method; autonomous GUI control is not evaluated.

name: Embodied Web Agents: Bridging Physical-Digital Realms for Integrated Agent Intelligence
summary: Introduces environments that couple 3D physical-world simulations with functional web interfaces. The accompanying benchmark evaluates tasks requiring agents to coordinate online information and physical actions across cooking, navigation and shopping scenarios.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The physical component is a simulation; the supported catalog connection is its functional web interaction.

name: Machine-Readable Ads: Accessibility and Trust Patterns for AI Web Agents interacting with Online Advertisements
summary: Compares DOM-based and pixel-based web agents on a cloned news site containing advertisements, consent dialogs and paywalls. The study examines how interface presentation affects ad interaction and consequential subscription choices.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Cognitive Duality for Adaptive Web Agents
summary: Introduces CogniWeb, which switches between fast reactive processing and slower deliberative reasoning according to task complexity. WebArena experiments examine this combination of learned behaviors and online planning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Throttling Web Agents Using Reasoning Gates
summary: Introduces reasoning gates that require agents to solve generated, verifiable puzzles before receiving access to resources. The throttling approach is deployed on a custom website and MCP servers and evaluated with web agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The contribution is an access-cost mechanism spanning websites and MCP servers, not a GUI navigation policy.

name: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
summary: Introduces OmniActor, which shares shallow model layers while separating deeper parameters to train jointly on GUI and embodied interactions. A unified action representation and mixed training data support evaluation in both task families.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Secure and Efficient Access Control for Computer-Use Agents via Context Space
summary: Introduces CSAgent, which combines static access policies with user intent and context and enforces them through an operating-system service. A supporting toolchain constructs and refines policies for agents using API, CLI and GUI interfaces.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
summary: Introduces WAInjectBench with a threat-model taxonomy and malicious and benign text-image datasets for web-agent prompt-injection detection. It compares detector families across explicit and less visible forms of injected content.

The reported contribution evaluates attack detection; end-to-end prevention of browser-agent compromise is not inferred.

name: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
summary: Introduces Behavior Judge, which converts execution trajectories into behavior narratives and compares multiple candidate rollouts. Experiments examine this selection approach on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AndroidWorld.

name: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks

name: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation

name: From Imperative to Declarative: Towards LLM-friendly OS Interfaces for Boosted Computer-Use Agents

name: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
summary: Introduces SecureWebArena with simulated interactive websites, an attack-vector taxonomy and labeled agent trajectories. Its evaluation separates failures in reasoning, behavioral traces and task outcomes across vision-language agent families.

name: BrowserAgent: Building Web Agents with Human-Inspired Web Browsing Actions

name: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents

name: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
summary: Introduces HackWorld for evaluating visual computer-use agents in a capture-the-flag collection of web applications. The benchmark examines interface navigation and multistep planning during vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks.

name: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers

name: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs

name: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
summary: Presents LiteAgent for recording web-agent interactions and TrickyArena for enabling or disabling dark patterns in controlled websites. Experiments compare how individual patterns, combined patterns and visual or HTML changes affect agent decisions.

name: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
summary: Introduces WebGraphEval, which merges multiple agents' trajectories into a weighted graph of canonical actions. Structural analyses examine recurring behavior, inefficient paths and important decision points beyond a final success score.

name: MGA: Memory-Driven GUI Agent for Observation-Centric Interaction

name: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding

name: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision

name: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent

name: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance

name: MEGA-GUI: Multi-stage Enhanced Grounding Agents for GUI Elements

name: AFRAgent : An Adaptive Feature Renormalization Based High Resolution Aware GUI agent

name: GAIR: GUI Automation via Information-Joint Reasoning and Group Reflection

name: WebSTAR: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering

name: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents

name: Training Computer Use Agents to Assess the Usability of Graphical User Interfaces
summary: uxCUA learns to assess interface usability by choosing interaction flows, executing them and predicting a numerical usability score. Training uses interactive UIs with usability labels and human preferences, with evaluations on synthetic and real interfaces.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.
verify_terms: Invisible in Space, Visible in T
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Gated Hindsight Distillation gives a teacher access to the next screenshot during training while the student sees only the available trajectory prefix. Distillation is applied when hindsight repairs a student failure, and the resulting policies are evaluated on Android tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: "Allow" to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
summary: This permission-literacy study tests whether mobile GUI agents grant only task-necessary permissions. Controlled changes to task context and requester identity expose authorization biases and the trade-off between suppressing unnecessary and legitimate grants.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
summary: This benchmark matches desktop goals, initial states and final-state verifiers across screen-only GUI and skill-mediated CLI agents. Its experiments separate graphical execution failures from missing CLI skill coverage, including a verifier-guided skill-augmentation condition.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks
summary: ChainWorld composes compatible atomic OSWorld tasks into multi-objective desktop chains while preserving their evaluators. It compares giving the full sequence at once with revealing goals turn by turn, exposing different state and session-management failures.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.
verify_terms: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enoug
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: MacArena: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on an Online macOS Environment
summary: MacArena runs computer-use tasks through Apple’s virtualization framework on Apple Silicon, combining task ports with macOS-native workloads. It distinguishes the ported and native subsets when examining agent performance and cross-platform transfer.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.
verify_terms: Online Skill Learning for Web Ag
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
summary: CLI-Anything argues for application interfaces built around structured commands, explicit state and execution feedback. It describes transforming existing software into command-line harnesses and organizing that approach through CLI-Hub.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Adjacent computer-interface architecture: the described application command harnesses concern computer operation, but no GUI execution or comparative benchmark result is established in the abstract.

name: Multi-Agent Computer Use
summary: MACU represents computer-use objectives as a dependency graph whose manager dispatches parallel subagents and revises tasks as new information arrives. Desktop and web experiments examine coordination, information handoff and task-completion time.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents
summary: UI-KOBE explores mobile applications to build graphs of UI states and executable transitions. A lightweight agent then matches its current screenshot to the graph and chooses a transition, local action, completion signal or fallback action.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
summary: MobileExplorer probes relevant UI elements while an on-device model is reasoning, then supplies the exploration trace as compact context. A two-level rollback mechanism restores the working state when simple backtracking fails.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
summary: DRS-GUI searches screenshot regions through focus, shift and scatter operations selected by a tree-search planner. A region-quality reward guides this training-free perceptual search before final GUI grounding.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.
notes: The complete retained official abstract and cached official README were reviewed. The README establishes browser execution against running SaaS applications; no repository code was executed and benchmark results were not independently reproduced.

name: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
summary: ToolCUA synthesizes interleaved GUI/tool trajectories and trains agents to choose between graphical actions and higher-level tools. Staged supervised and reinforcement learning culminate in online hybrid-environment training with a reward for efficient execution paths.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings, rather than establishing universal runtime prevention.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Do LLMs Need to See Everything? A Benchmark and Study of Failures in LLM-driven Smartphone Automation using Screentext vs. Screenshots
summary: DailyDroid compares text-only and text-plus-screenshot agents on everyday Android tasks across multiple apps and difficulty levels. Its failure analysis examines accessibility, observation modality and agent/application behavior.
verify_terms: Do LLMs Need to See Everything?
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
summary: This study examines repeated OSWorld executions to separate execution stochasticity, task-specification ambiguity and behavioral variation. Paired task-level tests show why one successful run is insufficient evidence of reliable computer use.
verify_terms: On the Reliability of Computer U
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
summary: UI-Copilot separates GUI execution from on-demand memory retrieval and numerical assistance. Its training procedure treats tool selection and multi-turn task execution as distinct optimization targets while keeping persistent observations outside transient context.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.
verify_terms: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? A
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.
verify_terms: Learn How to Act from Your Own I
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
summary: BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
